sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Channel function NOT affected by HA tag insertion in the Kir1.1/KCNJ1 extracellular loop (L4, citing Yoo et al. 2003); surface display of the tagged full-length rat ROMK construct confirmed in yeast (L1).
sites.rationale: [Literature audit 2026-11-05 (deliverome-analysis PR 236), verdict region_only: insert_after_residue 113 -> NULL; the paper names a region, not a junction (region: extracellular domain at Y113 of rat ROMK (human H113; junction 112|113 or 113|114 not stated)). validation_level surface_and_function -> detected_only (paper reports surface: not_reported, function: not_reported). Paper (PMID 39024255): "contained a single HA tag (GGYPYDVPDYAGG) inserted at Y113 in the extracellular domain". Audit note: Secondary source Yoo et al. 2003 JBC (PMID 12684516, doi 10.1074/jbc.M212301200) is not accessible: no PMC version, jbc.org and ScienceDirect return HTTP 403. Other Welling-lab papers tried: O'Connell 2005 PNAS (PMC1175014) blocked (PMC reCAPTCHA, pnas.org 403, Europe PMC XML 500); Fang 2009 JCI (PMID 19841541) is open but only says rat ROMK1 with an external HA epitope 'as described before', no residue. Quote above is from the original paper (PMC11449386). 'Inserted at Y113' still leaves 112|113 vs 113|114 (+-1) unresolved on human P48048 (H113).] Rat ROMK (Kir1.1/KCNJ1) and human KCNJ1 are orthologs of the same gene; the rat paper (L1) names Y113 as the insertion site in the single extracellular loop (residues 106–156 by computed landmarks), and human KCNJ1 has H at the same position 113 — a conservative species substitution at an identical structural location. Python confirms position 113 is H in the human sequence, 8 residues from TM1 end (105) and 44 from TM2 start (157), satisfying the ≥3-residue boundary constraint. L4 provides direct functional validation for KCNJ1 (Kir1.1): HA tag insertion in this loop does not affect channel function. L1: HA tag (GGYPYDVPDYAGG, 13 aa) inserted at Y113 in the extracellular domain of rat ROMK (Kir1.1/KCNJ1), a close ortholog of human KCNJ1; full-length surface-displayed channel expressed in yeast. Human KCNJ1 carries H at position 113 (species variant at the same structural position; same residue number). L4 (same PMC) additionally states that HA tag insertion in the Kir1.1 (KCNJ1) extracellular loop 'has been demonstrated not to affect the function' of the channel, citing Yoo et al. 2003.
sites.residue_label: extracellular domain at Y113 of rat ROMK (human H113; junction 112|113 or 113|114 not stated)

sources.claim: The rat ROMK-K80M construct used in the preliminary random mutagenesis screens contained a single HA tag (GGYPYDVPDYAGG) inserted at Y113 in the extracellular domain ( Yoo et al. , 2003 ), and its use in yeast expression studies was previously reported ( O’Donnell et al. , 2017 ; Mackie et al. , 2018 ).
sources.title: Characterization of hyperactive mutations in the renal potassium channel ROMK uncovers unique effects on channel biogenesis and ion conductance
